proposed_solution: Add companion tooling that extracts Buddy quest and questline page data into reviewable local outputs for requirements, rewards, gates, previous/next links, aliases, and source URLs.
scope_v1: Tooling and reviewed local outputs only; no runtime scraping; stop on structural ambiguity; missing item recognition should warn; do not bulk-promote unreviewed data into canonical app inputs.
notes: Shipped a respectful Buddy quest page-data extraction workflow with target CSV input, 3s default delay, JSON output, review CSV, and reviewable quest catalog/requirement/reward CSV rows. Ambiguous page structures stay marked for review instead of being promoted into canonical quest data.
friendly_summary: Extract Buddy quest data locally.
friendly_description: Create a respectful local Buddy quest extraction path that produces reviewed CSVs for quest planning without live app fetching.

title: Quest planner shared resource integration
user_value: Make quest progress use the same available-supply and target-output math as the broader resource planner.
proposed_solution: Adapt selected quest requirements into the shared target-output planning problem and consume the normalized available-supply layer including current inventory imports and override rules.
scope_v1: Adapter/model only; do not invent a parallel quest supply engine; keep direct quest progress usable while recursive craft and source planning mature; preserve provenance by source channel.
notes: Shipped a shared quest resource adapter and Quest Planner section that feeds active/watched quest requirements into the target-output planner, spends shared supply once, expands craft inputs, preserves quest-name contribution labels, and keeps direct quest progress rows intact.
friendly_summary: Use shared supply math for quests.
friendly_description: Feed quest requirements into the shared resource planner so quest demand and current inventory are compared consistently.
release_notes: Added shared resource planning to quests so active and watched requirements use the same pooled supply and craft-expansion math as the Target Planner.

title: Quest bottleneck source-pressure expansion
user_value: Show when multiple quests compete for the same scarce acquisition resource such as Large Nets or a hard explore location.
proposed_solution: Expand quest bottlenecks from direct missing items into grouped source pressure using reviewed drop-rate/source coverage and preferred units.
scope_v1: Bottleneck derivation only; source rows are advisory when coverage is partial; keep missing source data warning-safe; do not optimize routes or override user-selected priorities.
notes: Shipped source-pressure expansion that uses shared resource-plan missing rows first, groups reviewed drop-rate rows by source plus preferred unit, estimates source units when local rates support it, and falls back to source hints when coverage is partial. Use cases include DI XII Strange Rings and DI XIII Frost Snapper Shells competing for fishing or Large Net capacity.
friendly_summary: Group quest demand by scarce source.
friendly_description: Show shared pressure across selected quests so competing fishing, explore, pet, or crafting resources are obvious.
release_notes: Grouped selected quest gaps by shared source pressure using reviewed drop-rate rows and preferred units, with source-hint fallback when data is partial.

title: Quest synergy hint derivation
user_value: Surface useful overlap such as Black Rock Canyon helping PSA Orange Gecko demand while also producing Salt Rock for a nearby Salt Tower need.
proposed_solution: Add advisory synergy hints that connect quest demand to other watched quests, Tower targets, mastery goals, or selected item goals through shared sources and known recipe links.
scope_v1: Advisory hints only; no full route optimizer; do not let synergies override closest-useful ranking until prioritization modes are explicit; show uncertainty when source or recipe coverage is partial.
notes: Shipped drop-rate-backed same-source tower synergies. The first covered example is Orange Gecko from Black Rock Canyon surfacing Salt Rock into Salt for the Tower when Black Rock Canyon source rows are available.
friendly_summary: Show useful overlap while gathering.
friendly_description: Point out when working one quest source also advances another quest, Tower item, mastery target, or selected resource goal.

title: Quest prioritization and reward search modes
user_value: Let users choose whether to work closest quests, unlock chains, selected questlines, or reward-driven goals.
proposed_solution: Add prioritization controls for closest useful, selected chain, unlock-chain priority, manual quest set, and reward/item search once the core planner is trustworthy.
scope_v1: Ranking/search UI only; preserve manual selection; do not hide the assumptions behind each ranking; keep reward search local and source-linked.
notes: Shipped Quest Picker modes for chain order, closest local progress, scary future blockers, and local reward item search. Manual quest status remains authoritative.
friendly_summary: Choose quest ranking modes.
friendly_description: Add ranking and reward-search modes for quest planning after the direct progress and synergy model is stable.

title: Quest planner backup and restore durability

friendly_description: Make active, watched, completed, and hidden quest choices part of the normal local backup and restore flow.

title: Scary future quest requirement watchlist
user_value: Warn players about far-future quest blockers that deserve hoarding or early planning before they become the active quest problem.

It evaluates reviewed future and watched quests separately from active planning, includes recursive craft demand and current supply, and uses source-pressure rows where available. PSA Lima Beans/Spades still require future reviewed quest data before they can appear.
friendly_summary: Watch future quest blockers before they hurt.
friendly_description: Track scary future quest requirements separately from active quests so players know what to hoard, what passive sources will not cover, and which long-term blockers deserve early attention.
